newsitem.title: INDIA: India politician resigns over corruption scandal.
newsitem.headline: India politician resigns over corruption scandal.

text.p: A scandal-tainted Indian politician who has transfixed the nation for weeks resigned on Friday as chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar after his arrest was first ordered and then stayed.
In a sign that Laloo Prasad Yadav's exit did not mean the end of the controversy, his supporters promptly rubber-stamped his wife Rabri Devi as his successor.

Devi is not an elected official, and the hasty elevation of the housewife sparked widespread criticism. Rajesh Pilot, a leader of the Congress party, said Devi's appointment was a "mockery of democracy".
"I am happy," the 45-year-old mother of nine said nervously after she was sworn in. "I will pursue the policies of the Laloo government. Social justice will be the priority."
Bihar is India's second most populous state and one of its poorest regions.

Yadav resigned after a special court issued arrest warrants against him and three other politicians. India's Supreme Court said he should not be arrested until July 29 when it hears his appeal against the detention order.
The charismatic Yadav had stubbornly refused to resign since his indictment by the Central Bureau of Investigation in April.
"I did not want to create a constitutional crisis and people at the top had become critical of my stand not to resign," Yadav told reporters after his wife took office.
"Now I am free and I am ready to go to jail," he added. "The political and legal battle will go on."
The $280 million scandal involving the siphoning off of state farming funds has sharply divided Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition.
Leaders of Gujral's 15-party United Front were meeting in New Delhi late on Friday evening to decide on whether to retain Yadav's group in its fold.

"I welcome the resignation," Muthuvel Karunanidhi, leader of the regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam party, told Reuters in New Delhi. His party, upset with hardliners seeking Yadav's exit, had threatened to quit the coalition earlier this month.
Yadav's intransigence sparked a parliamentary uproar and a national debate on the conduct of leaders, and repeatedly rattled stock markets.
Friday's drama overshadowed the swearing-in of India's 10th president, K.R. Narayanan, who called for action to root out "the demon of corruption."
"Today there are signs of a weakening of the moral and spiritual fibre in our public life with the evils of communalism, casteism, violence and corruption bedevilling our society," Narayanan said.
Opposition lawmakers pressing for action against Yadav walked out of parliament's upper house while the lower house was angrily debating the scandal.
"The solution is in striking out the root of corruption," Somnath Chatterjee, leader of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), told the lower house, the Lok Sabha.
"It is in creating some convention and that is if there is any charge of corruption, he (the person accused) should step down and prove his innocence in the court," Chatterjee said.
The Yadav news shook up India's premier Bombay Stock Exchange, which fell sharply but then recovered some ground to close 36.76 points, or 0.87 percent, down at 4189.81.
